I've implemented support for custom `<signature>` and `<stamp>` block-level tags in the markdown conversion pipeline. All changes are confined to the single source file `docling/backend/md_backend.py`.

## What I did

**The problem:** marko parses `<signature>TEXT</signature>` not as an HTML block, but as *inline HTML* inside a paragraph — an opening `InlineHTML` node, the inner text, and a closing `InlineHTML` node. Previously these tags fell into the catch-all `else` branch and were silently dropped, leaving only the bare text.

**The implementation** (`docling/backend/md_backend.py`):

1. **Recognition** — Added `_CUSTOM_TAGS` plus regexes and a `_match_custom_tag()` helper that detects a paragraph whose first/last children are matching `<signature>`/`<stamp>` inline-HTML tags (case-insensitive, tolerates attributes), and extracts the enclosed text via a recursive `_collect_text()`.

2. **Hook point** — Right after the `visited` check in `_iterate_elements`, custom tags are intercepted *before* the generic paragraph/inline-group handling, so they're processed in document order and then the branch returns (children aren't re-processed).

3. **Document representation** — `_create_custom_tag_picture()` calls `doc.add_picture(...)`, sets `meta.classification.predictions[0].class_name` to `"signature"`/`"stamp"` (via `PictureMeta`/`PictureClassificationMetaField`/`PictureClassificationPrediction`), and adds the inner text as a child `TextItem` with both `text` and `orig` set.

## Verified behavior

- `<signature>John Doe</signature>` → `Signature\n\n<!-- image -->`
- `<stamp>APPROVED 2024</stamp>` → `Stamp\n\n<!-- image -->` (the humanized class name is emitted by docling_core's markdown serializer before the placeholder)
- Text preserved in `orig` + `text` on the picture's child; classification set correctly
- Body ordering preserved — text and picture elements interleave in input order
- Existing markdown backend tests still pass (2 passed)
- Edge cases handled: case-insensitivity, empty content, and non-block inline usage falls through to normal text handling
